name: First-floor en-suite shower room

dimensions.notes: Scaled from the 1:50 survey — approx. ±10 cm. Ceiling height as surveyed.

orientation: Small window (≈0.5 × 0.5 m) onto the angled side

current.summary: Existing: a tiny room in the front-left corner off the main room (door 0.77 × 1.87 m), with a small window onto the triangular void beside via Pietra Rossa. To become the en-suite shower room (see proposed works).
issues: Very tight — every centimetre counts; true wall positions unknown until plaster is stripped

proposal.summary: The tiny side room is rebuilt as an en-suite shower room for the bedroom, with a new pipe shaft in the triangular void behind it. Two layouts drawn:

options.name: Option A (Tavola 2)
options.detail: Shower 70 × 85 cm in the far corner; round basin on a wooden top; WC along the angled wall with a recessed cabinet (with door) above it; pipe shaft in the triangle.

options.name: Option B (Tavola 2/B)
options.detail: Shower in a niche at the back (≈0.52 × 0.80 m) — plaster to be stripped back to the brick to win every centimetre; WC in the middle (0.87 m bay, 0.45 m clear); basin on a wooden surface at the front (0.87 × 0.70 m) with mirror over; mosaic-tiled floor.

items: New pipe shaft (in the triangular void) taking waste down to ground floor
questions: Which option do you prefer? Option B gives a proper basin area; Option A a slightly bigger shower
Strip plaster to brick first (Option B note) so we know the real shower size
